what_it_does: Neurosymbolic AI blends two styles of reasoning: neural networks (which learn patterns from data) and symbolic reasoning (which applies logical rules, like a Prolog program or probabilistic inference). These combined workloads are notoriously hard for conventional hardware — CPUs, GPUs, and TPUs (Google's AI chips) all waste significant capacity because the two reasoning styles have very different memory and computation profiles. CogSys is a purpose-built chip design with three interlocked pieces: a mathematical technique to shrink the memory footprint of the symbolic reasoning part; a reconfigurable grid of small processing units that can switch mode between neural and symbolic computation; and a runtime scheduler that watches the current workload mix and assigns tasks to the right kind of unit. The design was evaluated at 28-nanometer silicon scale.
